document.title: The Verification Framework
document.subtitle: A reusable pattern for human-curated data across Business Hub, proposed as infrastructure beneath the AAR module
document.status: NOT YET ADOPTED — proposal in response to PRD v1.1 and ADR-001
document.important_caveat: This is a DESIGN PROPOSAL, not an implementation ticket. It argues for reframing verification as platform infrastructure and would materially change the build approach in several existing tickets (notably BH-1159, BH-1249, and the per-object Record Type pattern). Do NOT treat as build spec unless/until adopted.

problem_statement.thesis: Verification is treated as an AAR feature. It should be treated as Business Hub infrastructure.

arguments.name: Pattern keeps being reinvented
arguments.detail: Every module that ingests authoritative data and asks humans to curate it hits the same problem: AAR, ethics, COI, grant budget review, faculty appointments. AAR v1 solves it bespoke — the next module solves it bespoke again.

arguments.name: Research integrity is load-bearing
arguments.detail: 'System says X' and 'PI attested to X after review' are legally and institutionally different statements. Research Strategy exports to CIHR, Tri-Council, and rankings need provenance — not just values.

arguments.name: Trust breaks silently across cycles
arguments.detail: If a PI corrects an author attribution in 2026 and Wellspring re-syncs it back in 2027, the credibility of the entire suggest-verify offer collapses. The most influential users notice first.

core_idea.summary: Three states, one rule, one shared service

states.name: SUPERSEDED
states.description: Manual record displaced by a later-appearing source record (transition state)

core_idea.reconciliation_rule: When a source system updates a record the PI has already verified, the source wins ONLY if the PI has not yet attested. After verification, overrides are durable — the source cannot silently overwrite human judgment. Changes upstream are surfaced as events, never applied in place.

shared_service.name: VerificationReconciliationService
shared_service.principle: Every verifiable object's trigger calls this service. Not per-object logic.

shared_data_model.description: Applied consistently to every verifiable object via custom metadata

fields.purpose: Which authoritative system the record came from
Link back to source system record
Hash of source fields at last sync — detects upstream drift
Field-level PI corrections, read via merge-at-display

key_design_decision.rationale: Rather than duplicating every source field into an 'AAR version,' overrides live as a JSON document (e.g. {"title": "Corrected", "role": "Senior Author"}). Read-time merge: display = source_value ?? override_value.
benefits: New overrideable fields require zero schema migration

sync_reconciliation_cases.action: Silently update the proposed record. Refresh hash. PI has not yet engaged — safe to overwrite.
DO NOT OVERWRITE. Write a Verification_Change_Event. Optionally notify the PI. The verified record stays as-is.

sync_reconciliation_cases.trigger: Verification_Status__c = Manual, matching source record appears
sync_reconciliation_cases.action: Mark the manual record Superseded. Create a new Proposed record. Let the PI decide whether to merge.
Log to Verification_Change_Event__c. Every state change is auditable.

change_event_log.feeds: Bulk export Research Strategy already wants (EXP-03)
transitions_captured: Verified → Verified + override (PI corrected a field)
Source changed under Verified (upstream drift, surfaced not applied)

unlocks.detail: Read directly from the event log — no runtime diffing
Override rates by institute. Source-system disagreement rates. Time-to-verify.
'Was this value PI-attested or system-suggested?' — one click, one query
Override durability across AAR cycles becomes observable, not just promised

lwc_component.name: c-verification-card
lwc_component.scope: One reusable component. Drop onto any record page. Works in Experience Cloud.

inputs.name: fieldSetName
inputs.purpose: which fields to show and make editable

built_in_behaviours: Proposed rows muted with a Verify button
Verified rows editable, 'corrected' indicator on overrides
Verify All bulk action — satisfies SUB-06 as a component, not a screen flow
Hover on override shows source value + timestamp

architecture_layers.summary: Three horizontal layers. AAR is the first tenant. The next module drops in at the top without touching anything below.

layers.name: Service
components: VerificationReconciliationService (Apex) — encodes the reconciliation rule, writes change events on transitions, enforces override durability

layers.name: Audit log
components: Verification_Change_Event__c — append-only, feeds EXP-03 bulk export and trust metrics

layers.name: Source systems (read-only authoritative)
layers.principle: Authoritative. Never mutated by AAR overrides.

strategic_case_beyond_aar.detail: AAR, ethics review, conflict-of-interest disclosure, grant budget review, faculty appointments, safety reporting. Each module after AAR is cheaper.

strategic_case_beyond_aar.theme: A defensible answer to 'how do we know this is trustworthy?'
strategic_case_beyond_aar.detail: Research Strategy, TRBS, and eventually external auditors will ask. The event log is the answer: every value in Business Hub has a provenance chain.

strategic_case_beyond_aar.theme: An analytics layer you can't build retroactively
strategic_case_beyond_aar.detail: Override rates, source-system disagreement rates, time-to-verify, engagement trends. High-value signals for institute leadership — but only if the event object exists from day one.

recommended_next_steps.total_effort: ~2 weeks of additional design and abstraction work before Q1 build

tasks.title: Formalize the pattern above AAR
tasks.action: Write a one-page internal design note: 'Business Hub Verification Framework.' Get Robert Chen's signoff. Elevates the pattern above AAR and sets precedent for every module after it.

tasks.title: Build the service and component as platform code
tasks.action: c-verification-card and VerificationReconciliationService ship as standalone deliverables with their own test coverage, separate from the AAR feature branch. Treat them as infrastructure, not AAR code.

tasks.title: Prototype against publications first
tasks.action: Publications are the hardest case — multi-author, junction-based verification on UHN_Publication_Author__c. If the pattern works there, it works for grants, awards, supervision, and everything that comes after.

closing_argument: Build verification once. Ship it as platform. Let AAR be its first tenant. Cost: two weeks of design and abstraction. Return: every future Business Hub module gets verification UX and auditability for the cost of a page layout change.

BH-1159.ticket_approach: Record Types per object (Proposed / Verified / Manual Entry) with different page layouts per type. Per-object configuration.
BH-1159.proposal_approach: Single Verification_Status__c picklist field on all verifiable objects, driven by a shared Apex service. One LWC handles UI across objects.
BH-1159.conflict: Different architectures. Picking the proposal would make BH-1159's Record Types redundant (state would live on a picklist field, not a Record Type).

BH-1249.ticket_approach: Per-object Screen Flows (mini-Flows) that transition Record Types Proposed → Verified
BH-1249.proposal_approach: Shared LWC + Apex service. No per-object Flows.
BH-1249.conflict: Picking the proposal would replace BH-1249's Flow work with a single LWC + service.

BH-987 (AAR_Recognition__c).ticket_approach: Manual entry only — no source system, no verification fields
BH-987 (AAR_Recognition__c).proposal_approach: Still supports Manual as a state; the framework adds nothing to manual-only objects, so no conflict — Recognition simply lives at Manual without sync reconciliation.

BH-1126.ticket_approach: Tracks Source__c, Is_Verified__c on AAR_Publication__c. Field-history audit for verification state.
BH-1126.proposal_approach: Audit lives in Verification_Change_Event__c, not field history. The proposed Verified_By__c / Verified_At__c fields cover the same provenance the ticket tries to capture via field history.
BH-1126.conflict: Partial overlap. Picking the proposal would let BH-1126 drop some field-history tracking in favour of the event log.

publications_special_case.alignment: Both BH-1159 and this proposal agree verification state lives on the junction UHN_Publication_Author__c, not on the publication record. Multi-author handling matches.
